stem: Meera plants a bean seed in a pot at her home in Pune. She turns the pot upside down so that the germinating seedling is inverted, and keeps it near a window where sunlight comes from the right side. After a few days, what will she observe about the direction of growth of the root and the shoot?

options.text: The root keeps growing upward and the shoot keeps growing downward, in the directions they were already pointing.
The root grows downward and the shoot grows upward, bending towards the sunlight.
The root bends towards the sunlight and the shoot grows downward.
Both the root and the shoot bend towards the sunlight coming from the right.

teacher.key_rationale: Roots always grow downward (positive gravitropism) regardless of the seedling's orientation, while shoots grow upward and towards light. Even when the pot is inverted, the root re-orients to grow downward and the shoot grows upward towards the sunlight, so B is correct. Option A is the trap for students who think roots and shoots keep growing in whichever direction they are already pointing; C and D wrongly assign light-seeking behaviour to the root.
